items.followUp: Why is the value of g greater at the poles than at the equator?

accept: earth is not a perfect sphere
rubric.why: Award for explaining that Earth’s shape or rotation causes g to vary with latitude.
rubric.how: State that Earth’s shape and rotation make g different at different latitudes; g is greater at the poles than at the equator.

rubric.why: Award for identifying that g changes with distance from Earth’s centre.
rubric.how: State that g decreases as altitude above Earth’s surface increases.

modelAnswer: The value of g varies because Earth is not a perfect sphere and because of its rotation; g is greater at the poles than at the equator.
The value of g also decreases with increasing altitude above Earth’s surface.

items.followUp: State two environmental disadvantages of burning fossil fuels.

rubric.why: Award for identifying that fossil fuels are limited and cannot be replenished on a human timescale.
rubric.how: State that fossil fuels are non-renewable or finite.

rubric.why: Award for naming a harmful environmental effect of using fossil fuels.
rubric.how: Name an effect such as air pollution, global warming or acid rain.

modelAnswer: Fossil fuels are non-renewable, so their supplies are limited and will eventually run out.
Burning them causes pollution, including greenhouse-gas emissions that contribute to global warming.

items.followUp: Define gravitational potential energy and write its equation near Earth’s surface.

rubric.why: Award for defining kinetic energy as the energy associated with motion.
rubric.how: State that kinetic energy is the energy a body possesses because of its motion.

rubric.why: Award for the correct kinetic-energy equation.
rubric.how: Write KE = ½mv², with m as mass and v as speed.

modelAnswer: Kinetic energy is the energy possessed by a body due to its motion.
K.E. = ½mv², where m is the mass of the body and v is its speed.

items.followUp: Define efficiency and write its formula as a percentage.

accept: ratio of useful output to input
rubric.why: Award for describing efficiency as a comparison of useful output with input.
rubric.how: Define efficiency as the ratio of useful output to total input.

rubric.why: Award for the correct percentage formula.

modelAnswer: Efficiency is the ratio of useful output to total input.

items.followUp: Define matter and name its three common states.

rubric.why: Award for both defining properties of matter.
rubric.how: State that matter has mass and occupies space.

rubric.why: Award for naming all three states.

modelAnswer: Matter is anything that has mass and occupies space.
The three common states of matter are solid, liquid and gas.

items.followUp: Define density and write its formula.

rubric.why: Award for defining pressure in terms of force and area.
rubric.how: State that pressure is the force acting per unit area.

modelAnswer: Pressure is the force acting per unit area.
Pressure, P = force, F ÷ area, A; therefore P = F/A.

items.followUp: A wire of original length 2 m extends by 0.01 m. Calculate its strain.

rubric.why: Award for defining strain as a comparison of extension with original length.
rubric.how: State that strain is the change in length divided by the original length.
Write strain = change in length ÷ original length.

modelAnswer: Strain is the ratio of the change in length of a body to its original length.
Strain = change in length ÷ original length = Δl/l.

items.followUp: What are the lower and upper fixed points on the Celsius scale, and what temperatures do they represent?

rubric.why: Award for identifying the lower fixed point and its temperature.
rubric.how: State that the lower fixed point is the ice point, 0°C, at standard atmospheric pressure.

rubric.why: Award for identifying the upper fixed point and its temperature.
rubric.how: State that the upper fixed point is the steam point, 100°C, at standard atmospheric pressure.

modelAnswer: The lower fixed point is the ice point: the temperature of melting ice at standard atmospheric pressure, taken as 0°C.
The upper fixed point is the steam point: the temperature of steam above boiling water at standard atmospheric pressure, taken as 100°C.
